summary: The code change is real and I could not knock it over. I independently reproduced everything the agent claimed: the banner now reads the partner's own page list before it says anything, the words on screen and the link destination are the same place, and the public 404 page keeps a genuine privacy property (all three miss cases return byte-identical HTML, verified 889 bytes each). No drive-by edits, no journey -intended touched, no money handling, no new outbound call, no secrets. File scope is exactly clean: the only three code files carrying this unit's T10-01 tag are the three it claims. What fails: (a) the main fix — the Home banner — has ZERO automated test coverage; the only proof is a home-grown probe script, which I ran and which reproduces the recorded output byte-for-byte, but a probe is not a test that CI will run; (b) 3 of the 6 new tests pass identically against the old code, so they prove nothing about the fix — I proved this by mutating the handler back to the old 404 body and watching tests 1, 4 and 5 stay green; (c) all 6 new tests live in a .pg.test.mjs, which SKIPS in the blocking CI job (no DATABASE_URL) and only runs in the non-blocking Postgres job — meanwhile a no-database test file for this exact handler already exists (src/http/partner-site-function.test.mjs) and was not extended, so the new 404 wording can silently regress with the merge gate still green; (d) the new test cannot run as the unprivileged fundhub_app role at all — its setup hook is blocked by row-level security and all 6 tests cancel, where a comparable existing pg test degrades to 39/40; (e) docs/journeys/white-label-actual.md and CHANGELOG.md are owed per CLAUDE.md sections 4 and 6, which the agent disclosed and could not do. In plain words: the fix works and it is honest, but almost nothing automatic will notice if someone breaks it later.

violations.what: The primary user-visible change — the Home banner in partner-galaxy.html — has no automated test at all. Every one of the 6 new tests exercises the API and the public /sites/ handler; not one loads or asserts the banner. The only evidence is a hand-written probe script in the evidence folder. I ran it and it reproduces the recorded JSON byte-for-byte, and it genuinely extracts the live code block out of the HTML by regex rather than reimplementing it, so it is honest evidence — but nothing in CI runs it. A Playwright e2e job exists and blocks (npm run test:e2e), and no spec was added to it. If someone breaks the banner tomorrow, every gate stays green.
violations.evidence: showOwnUrl() at line 1743 is the fix. `grep -rn showOwnUrl src/ e2e/` finds nothing. Only docs/workflows/fix-2026-08-18/evidence/T10/C-partner-page/banner-render-probe.mjs touches it, and that file is documentation, not a test.

violations.what: 3 of the 6 new tests pass identically against the old code, so they are characterization tests, not proof of a fix. I mutated netlify/functions/partner-site.mjs to return the OLD 404 body (keeping the export so the import still resolved), re-ran, and restored the file byte-for-byte afterwards.
violations.evidence: Mutant run output: ok 1 'a draft page is NOT served to the public'; not ok 2 'the miss page says what a draft is'; not ok 3 'SECURITY: real id indistinguishable'; ok 4 'Brand Studio reports live_path as NULL'; ok 5 'pressing Publish makes that address live'; not ok 6. Tests 1, 4 and 5 bite nothing. Tests 3 and 6 only failed because they compare to the new NOT_LIVE_HTML string — the security property they assert held under the old code too, so they are regression guards, not fix proof.

violations.what: The new tests are placed where the merge gate will not run them. The whole suite is guarded by `skip: !HAVE_DB`, and .github/workflows/tests.yml runs the BLOCKING job with DATABASE_URL deliberately unset. The Postgres job that would run them carries `continue-on-error: true`. So the one assertion that actually bites — the new 404 wording — is only checked in a job that cannot fail the branch. A no-database test file for this exact handler already exists and imports it directly; the wording assertion belonged there and would have cost nothing.
violations.evidence: Line 38: `skip: !HAVE_DB ? "no DATABASE_URL" : false`. tests.yml line ~204: `continue-on-error: true` on the postgres job. src/http/partner-site-function.test.mjs already imports { handler, parsePath } from the same module and runs with no database (2/2 pass, confirmed).

violations.what: The new pg test cannot run as the unprivileged app role that production actually uses. Its before() hook inserts straight into partner_module_settings with no partner scope, and row-level security rejects it, cancelling all 6 tests. A comparable pre-existing pg test in the same directory degrades far more gracefully under the same role, so this is not simply 'how pg tests are here'.
violations.evidence: As fundhub_app on fundhub_t10_c: `error: 'new row violates row-level security policy for table "partner_module_settings"'`, code 42501, at test file line 80 — # pass 0, # cancelled 6. Same role, src/http/creative-endpoints.pg.test.mjs: # pass 39, # fail 1. As the owner role the new file is 6/6, which is how the agent measured it.

violations.check: 8. NO INVENTED GROUND TRUTH / CLAUDE.md sections 4 and 6
violations.what: No -intended.md was touched — that check is clean. But the required -actual journey update was not made. docs/journeys/white-label-actual.md (265 lines) contains no mention of the Home banner, the /sites/ miss page, or the draft-vs-published distinction, and docs/journeys/CHANGELOG.md has no new line. CLAUDE.md section 4 says this must land in the same commit as the code, and section 6 lists it as a definition-of-done gate. The agent disclosed this and correctly said it could not do it because the files were not in its owned list — so this is an orchestrator to-do, not misconduct, but the unit is not 'done' until it happens.
violations.evidence: `git diff --name-only docs/` returns nothing. `grep -n 'own-url|partner-galaxy|Your page|not published|partner-site' docs/journeys/white-label-actual.md` returns nothing.

violations.what: If the page-list read fails or is refused, the banner silently leaves the page's default text in place: 'Your page · sign in to see your address'. A partner who IS signed in then reads a caption telling them to sign in. It is not a fabricated number and it is not worse than before, but it is a wrong caption on a real failure path, and the probe evidence does not cover that fifth state.
violations.evidence:
Line 1775: `if (!items) return; // could not read it — do not guess`. Line 303: `
Your page · sign in to see your address
`. banner-render-probe.json records 4 states, all with a successful read.

violations.what: When a partner has more than one page, the banner shows whichever published page the API listed first — the API orders by updated_at DESC, so it is the most recently edited one, not necessarily the apply page. Before the change the banner always named the apply address. So a partner whose apply page is a draft but whose (say) thank-you page is live will see the thank-you address labelled 'Your page'. It is a true live address, so this is not a lie, but it is not necessarily the address they expect.
violations.evidence: Line 1782 loop takes the first item where status === 'published'; api/partner-pages.mjs GET orders `ORDER BY updated_at DESC` and does not filter by funnel_key or slug.
